answers.question: What was the task?
answers.answer: The task was to upgrade the logging library to version 2.
quotes: The task was to upgrade the logging library to version 2.

answers.question: How did it end: what is done and what is not?
answers.answer: The build now takes the new library version and that is the whole change; the operations team's file was not touched, and the project was not built and no tests were run, so the alert on errors no longer sees our error lines.
quotes: The build now takes the new version, and that is the whole change.
I did not touch the operations team's file. I did not build the project or run any tests.
So the operations team's alert on errors no longer sees our error lines.

answers.question: How does the thing that changed work?
answers.answer: The operations team's alert fires for every log line matching a pattern in their file, and that pattern expects the old time form (local time, a space, a comma before the milliseconds), while the new version writes UTC with a letter T and a dot.
quotes: It fires for every log line that matches a pattern in their file.
The pattern expects the old time form: local time, a space, a comma before the milliseconds.
The new version writes the time in UTC, with a letter T and a dot.

answers.question: What is the problem, and what causes it?
answers.answer: The new library version writes the time of each log line in a new form that the alert's pattern does not match, so if this ships as it is, errors raise no alert at all.
quotes: But the new version writes the time of each log line in a new form.
I ran their pattern on one error line written each way. It matched the old line and missed the new one.
So if this ships as it is, our errors raise no alert at all.

answers.question: What is not verified?
answers.answer: The project was not built and no tests were run; the only check made was running the alert pattern on one error line written each way.
quotes: I did not build the project or run any tests.
I ran their pattern on one error line written each way.

answers.missing: The text would have to say what decision the reader is being asked to take and list the options (for example ship as it is, keep the old time form, or change the alert pattern) with what each gives and costs; it only lists where to look.
